environment: This is a deterministic in-memory Node.js ESM model of two callers, not PostgreSQL isolation. Both calls reach await after their initial check before either resumes; A then resumes before B. Predict before running it; we can run it after your answer.

cases.surface: two callers decrement the final seat after a shared check
cases.question: Predict every printed line and both return values. Does the one-seat business rule hold? Identify the observation and update that can interleave.

criteria.description: Predicts two accepted results and a final seat count of -1.
Explains that both callers pass the availability check before either decrement and that two successful reservations violate the one-seat rule.

wrongModels.claim: Individual writes are atomic, so the earlier availability check and later decrement behave as one safe decision.

cases.surface: two successful reservations overwrite stock from the same stale read
cases.question: Predict every printed line and both return values. Can the final seat count by itself prove only one client reserved the seat? Explain the read/write interleaving.

criteria.description: Predicts two accepted results even though the final seat count is 0.
Explains that both callers read the same initial count and write back the same derived value, so final state hides the duplicate success.

wrongModels.claim: A nonnegative final stock proves only one reservation succeeded.

cases.surface: two clients claim one username while a Set hides duplicate writes
cases.question: Predict every printed line and both return values. Can the final Set by itself prove only one client received a successful claim? Explain which boundary matters.

criteria.description: Predicts two successful claims while the final Set contains only alex.
Explains that both clients observe absence before either add; unique final storage does not by itself guarantee one successful decision.

wrongModels.claim: Set uniqueness means the second client must be rejected.
